methodological_rigor.justification: The normalized manuscript contains only the title, 'Retraction Note: A water-soluble nucleolin aptamer-paclitaxel conjugate for tumor-specific targeting in ovarian cancer,' and provides no abstract, methods, results, statistics, or evidence for evaluation. Because no study design, sample, controls, endpoints, or analyses are described, methodological rigor cannot be established from the text. No statistical methods or results are reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The available text is a retraction-note title rather than a research manuscript, so the only supportable Oxford classification is level 5 because no original clinical or preclinical evidence is presented. Ovarian cancer drug-targeting with a nucleolin aptamer-paclitaxel conjugate could be clinically relevant in principle, but the normalized text provides no data, patient population, endpoints, or translational evidence. As presented, there is no assessable path to clinical impact.

reporting_quality.justification: No reporting standard can be applied because the normalized file contains only a retraction-note title and no manuscript content. Required elements such as rationale, design, methods, results, limitations, ethics, and statistical reporting are absent. There is no data availability, source data, repository, code, or reproducibility information in the text.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty cannot be credited from a retraction-note title alone. The text names a water-soluble nucleolin aptamer-paclitaxel conjugate in ovarian cancer but provides no findings, mechanism, model system, or positioning against prior literature. Because no evidence remains to support an original contribution, the appropriate novelty score is minimal.

writing_presentation.justification: The file has a clear title but lacks an abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, tables, references, or retraction rationale. With only five lines of normalized text, the manuscript cannot communicate scientific evidence or support review. Presentation is therefore fundamentally incomplete for publication assessment.
